name: Nawdm
world_status: statement found in an open source
sweep_summary: Nawdm (nawd1238) is not in the catalog. The single title hit, Nicole 1983 'Contribution à l'étude de faits prosodiques des unités phonologiques supérieures: exemple d'analyse d'une conversation en nawdm' (in Bearth ed., Perspectives dans l'analyse du discours, ILA/SIL Abidjan, pp. 153-87; Glottolog record opened and confirmed), is by its title and Glottolog subject a discourse-level prosody study of one conversation (units above the word), so prosody-but-not-word-stress; no open copy exists anywhere I could reach (archive.org 0 hits, Google Books not digitised, HathiTrust/WorldCat/sil.org blocked, no DOI), so it is library-print-only, priority low. The same author's 1979 'Esquisse phonologique du nawdm' (already on file from the earlier audit, archive.org Rosetta scan; pages 13-14 and 40-41 rendered and read visually) gives the first-hand word-stress statement: Nawdm has an intensity accent in addition to H/B tone; every noun, verb and adverb has at least one accented syllable; the phonological word = one principal accent; simple pronouns are unaccented; compounds take the principal accent on the last member with secondary accents earlier. No explicit placement rule for simplex words, but all simplex examples are initially accented. This is the recommended deciding source if Nawdm is added to the catalog (stress present + tone; initial by example; compound-final principal accent).org, Google Books, Crossref, Semantic Scholar [429], sil.org [403]).

new_statements.quote: On distingue en nawdm trois types de syllabes selon ce critères: les syllabes porteuses de l'accent principal, celles qui sont porteuses de l'accent secondaire, celles enfin qui ne portent aucun accent particulier. Dans tous les noms, tous les verbes, tous les adverbes, il y a au moins une syllabe accentuée (précédée de [']). Exemples: ['watʋ] "nuages" où la première syllabe est plus énergique que la deuxième. Dans les mots composés, c'est-à-dire construits à l'aide de plusieurs éléments, il y a souvent un accent principal et un accent secondaire (précédé de [,]). Exemples: [,da:'ku:da] "le buveur, l'ivrogne" composé de deux éléments: ['da:m] "boisson" et ['ku:da] "tueur"
new_statements.translation: In Nawdm one distinguishes three types of syllable by this criterion: syllables bearing the main accent, those bearing the secondary accent, and finally those bearing no particular accent. In every noun, every verb, every adverb there is at least one accented syllable (preceded by [']). Examples: ['watʋ] 'clouds', where the first syllable is more energetic than the second. In compound words, i.e. those built from several elements, there is often a main accent and a secondary accent (preceded by [,]). Examples: [,da:'ku:da] 'the drinker, the drunkard', composed of two elements: ['da:m] 'drink' and ['ku:da] 'killer'.
new_statements.citation: Nicole, Jacques. 1979. Esquisse phonologique du nawdm ou les bases d'une orthographe pratique de cette langue. Lomé: Institut National de la Recherche Scientifique / Société Internationale de Linguistique. 50 pp.
new_statements.locator: §1.4 'L'accent d'intensité', pp. 13-14 (PDF pages 13-14 of the archive.org scan); see also §3.2 'Le mot phonologique', pp. 40-41
new_statements.reading: tone language with a stress statement
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened via its ABBYY scanned (lines 616-653 and 3279-3305) and the saved page renders,,, read visually). The quoted passage is on printed pp. 13-14, section "1.4. L'ACCENT D'INTENSITE", exactly as quoted: "On distingue en nawdm trois types de syllabes selon ce critères: les syllabes porteuses de l'accent principal, celles qui sont porteuses de l'accent secondaire, celles enfin qui ne portent aucun accent particulier. Dans tous les noms, tous les verbes, tous les adverbes, il y a au moins une syllabe accentuée (précédée de [']). Exemples: ['watʋ] "nuages" où la première syllabe est plus énergique que la deuxième.... Dans les mots composés... il y a souvent un accent principal et un accent se…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Nawdm is a two-tone language (H/B, §2.5) that also has a stress ('accent d'intensité'). Nicole states that stress exists, that every noun/verb/adverb carries one main stress, that simple pronouns are unstressed clitics, and that compounds add secondary stresses, but gives NO explicit rule for the position of the main stress. Every simple-word example in the book is marked with stress on the first syllable ([\'watʋ], burgu, [\'da:m], [\'ku:da], [\'ti:bɛ], [\'di:tɛ], [\'do:bɛ], [\'kodgu], [\'rondɛ], [\'dabidɛ]), and in the compounds the main stress sits on the initial syllable of the last member ([,da:\'ku:da], [,baŋm,kpi:r\'bi:m]); this is consistent with stress on the first syllable of the (last) stem, but that is my inference from the examples, not a statement in the source.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Explicit: compounds often have a main accent plus one or two secondary accents (marked [,]), e.g. [,da:'ku:da]; [,baŋm,kpi:r'bi:m] 'amande de palmiste' with two secondaries (p. 14; repeated p. 41).
new_statements.exceptions: Simple pronouns (le/ve/te/ne etc.) bear no intensity accent and are therefore not phonological words (p. 41; also Gasser 1984 lesson 1.2). Allophony of /t d u ɔ e/ is conditioned on accented vs unaccented syllable (§2.3-2.4, pp. 19-38).
new_statements.domain_note: Word level: the phonological word is defined as 'une unité qui comporte un accent principal' (p. 40); examples are isolated citation forms. Tone is treated separately (three phonetic levels, two phonological tones, low distinctive load, not written in the orthography).
new_statements.identity_note: Nicole 1979 describes the Niamtougou variety (west group: Niamtougou, Koka, Baga), noting an east group (Canton de Siou) with good mutual intelligibility; Gasser 1984 is based on the Koka dialect. All fall under nawd1238 (no dialect glottocodes).

new_statements.quote: Toutes les syllabes d'un mot ne sont pas prononcées avec la même énergie, mais certaines sont plus accentuées que d'autres. On distingue en nawdm trois types de syllabes selon ce critères: les syllabes porteuses de l'accent principal, celles qui sont porteuses de l'accent secondaire, celles enfin qui ne portent aucun accent particulier. Dans tous les noms, tous les verbes, tous les adverbes, il y a au moins une syllabe accentuée (précédée de [']). Exemples: ['watʊ] "nuages" où la première syllabe est plus énergique que la deuxième. La première syllabe est accentuée la seconde ne l'est pas. (p. 13) [...] Le mot phonologique est défini comme une unité qui comporte un accent principal. (p. 40)
new_statements.translation: Not all syllables of a word are pronounced with the same energy; some are more accented than others. Nawdm distinguishes three syllable types on this criterion: syllables bearing the principal accent, those bearing the secondary accent, and those bearing no particular accent. In all nouns, all verbs and all adverbs there is at least one accented syllable (preceded by [']). Examples: ['watʊ] 'clouds', where the first syllable is more energetic than the second; the first syllable is accented, the second is not. [...] The phonological word is defined as a unit that carries one principal accent.
new_statements.citation: Nicole, Jacques (1979). Esquisse phonologique du nawdm ou les bases d'une orthographe pratique de cette langue. Lomé: Institut National de la Recherche Scientifique / Société Internationale de Linguistique. 50 pp.
new_statements.locator: §1.4 'L'accent d'intensité', pp. 13-14 (PDF pages 13-14); §3.2 'Le mot phonologique', pp. 40-41 (PDF pages 40-41)
new_statements.reading: Nawdm is described as having a genuine word-level intensity (dynamic) accent coexisting with two-level lexical tone: one principal accent per phonological word, obligatory in nouns/verbs/adverbs, absent from simple pronouns (which are therefore clitics), with secondary accents in compounds and the principal accent on the compound's last member ([ˌda:ˈku:da], [ˌbaŋmˌkpi:rˈbi:m]). The source states no positional rule for simplex words, but every simplex example it gives is initially accented ([ˈwatʊ], [ˈburgu], [ˈda:m], [ˈku:da]), so the best coding supported by the text is: stress present alongside tone, principal accent on the initial (root) syllable of simplex words by example only, rightmost member accented in compounds. A firmer placement rule would need Nicole 1980 (Phonologie et morphophonologie du nawdm, SIL) or Nicole 2018 (Grammaire du nawdm, SIL e-Books 69), both behind sil.org's 403.
